newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert rubbishes idea of stability council.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert rubbishes idea of stability council.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert on Tuesday dismissed a French proposal to create a "stability council" as a political counterweight to the future European Central Bank.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a reception in the eastern German city of Leipzig, Sievert said the question of the creation of such a council was one of the issues that had to be addressed in the run-up to European Economic Monetary Union.

"We must consider the problematic wish to confront the European Central Bank with a stability council, which should have a public debate...with the central bank concerning monetary policy and exchange rates," he said.

He added, according to a text of his speech, that this appeared to be a meaningless attempt to find some form of mediator for monetary policy, which has the clearly defined role of maintaining price stability as its absolute priority.

"Of course, once the European Central Bank has the power to take the role which the Maastricht Treaties have given it, there may be some comfort in the fact that a stability council, which has nothing to decide, would only make a fool of itself if it hit on the idea of suggesting that the moon should go in the oposite direction from that which is ordained," he said.
"But why then bother with such a council at all," he added.
The main idea behind the proposal for such a council is to have a political body, which examines the level of the euro's exchange rate against other major currencies.
